name: Oil & Filter Change
description: Your engine's most fundamental routine. Clean oil reduces internal wear, restores fuel efficiency and protects components between major services. We use the correct grade and specification for your exact vehicle.
includes: Drain and refill with manufacturer-specified oil grade
New OE-quality oil filter fitted
Oil level and pressure verified
Screen wash and coolant topped up if required

name: Interim Service
description: Recommended every six months or 6,000 miles, the interim service covers the critical safety and fluid checks that keep your car running safely and efficiently. Fast, thorough and always carried out to manufacturer specification.
includes: Engine oil and filter change
Brake system inspection (pads, discs, fluid level)
Tyre condition, pressure and tread depth check
All fluid levels inspected and topped up
Lights, wipers, horn and visual safety check

name: Full Service
description: A comprehensive annual service covering every major vehicle system to manufacturer specification. Recommended every twelve months or 12,000 miles — the most complete routine maintenance we carry out.
includes: All items from the Interim Service
Air filter and cabin pollen filter replacement
Spark plug inspection or replacement (petrol engines)
Full 52-point vehicle health check with written report
Fuel system condition and drive belt inspection

name: Major Service
description: The complete two-yearly or 24,000-mile service. Covers everything in the full service plus all long-interval components requiring scheduled attention, leaving your vehicle in the best possible mechanical condition.
includes: All items from the Full Service
Brake fluid change (if overdue or contaminated)
Coolant condition, concentration and pH check
Gearbox and differential fluid levels checked
Steering, suspension and drivetrain comprehensive inspection

name: MOT Test
description: DVSA-authorised annual roadworthiness test for cars (Class 4) and light vans (Class 7). We can carry out any required remedial work on the same day wherever possible, and re-tests are included when we complete the repair work.
includes: Full DVSA-standard MOT inspection
Written report of all findings, advisories and failures
Same-day remedial work wherever possible
Re-test included when repair carried out by us

name: Pre-MOT Inspection
description: A thorough pre-test check before your official MOT. We identify likely failures in advance so repairs can be completed beforehand — saving time, avoiding a failed certificate and significantly increasing first-time pass likelihood.
includes: Check of all MOT-relevant systems and components
Written advisory report on items likely to fail
Priority repair booking arranged before your test date
Gives you the option to address issues before the official test

name: MOT + Full Service
description: Our most popular combination. Booking your MOT alongside a full service is the most efficient use of your annual service visit — completing all required maintenance and the roadworthiness test in one appointment.
includes: Full DVSA-standard MOT test
Complete full service to manufacturer specification
Combined health check report
Any required remedial work quoted and booked on the day

name: Brake System Health Check
description: A comprehensive inspection of your entire braking system. We check pad and disc condition, fluid quality, caliper function, brake lines and handbrake performance — identifying issues before they become safety concerns.
includes: Front and rear brake pad wear measurement
Brake disc thickness, scoring and corrosion check
Brake fluid moisture content test
Caliper operation and handbrake function check

name: Brake Fluid Change
description: Brake fluid absorbs moisture over time, lowering its boiling point and causing brake fade under heavy use. Recommended every two years — one of the most overlooked yet critical safety maintenance items on any vehicle.
includes: Complete brake fluid bleed and refill
DOT 4 fluid used as standard (vehicle-specific grades available)
System pressurised and checked for leaks post-bleed
Pedal feel and handbrake function verified on completion

name: Front Brake Pad Replacement
description: Front brakes take the majority of braking force and wear faster than rears. We fit quality pads meeting or exceeding OEM specification, and always recommend inspecting disc condition at the same time.
includes: OEM-specification front brake pads fitted
Caliper slider pins cleaned and lubricated
Brake disc surface condition assessed
Brakes bedded in and pedal feel verified

name: Rear Brake Pad Replacement
description: Rear pads wear more slowly but are critical for balanced braking. On vehicles with electronic parking brakes (EPB), specialist tooling is required to retract the caliper pistons — which we carry as standard.
includes: OEM-specification rear brake pads fitted
Electric parking brake (EPB) retraction where applicable
Caliper slider pins cleaned and lubricated
Handbrake function verified on completion

name: Front Disc & Pad Replacement
description: When discs are worn beyond safe tolerance, replacement pads alone are not sufficient. We always recommend replacing discs and pads as a matched set for safe, even braking performance and maximum longevity.
includes: OEM-quality brake discs and pads fitted as a matched set
Hub face cleaned to prevent disc run-out
Caliper slider pins fully serviced and lubricated
Full road test carried out before vehicle handover

name: Rear Disc & Pad Replacement
description: Rear disc and pad replacement requires particular attention on vehicles with integrated handbrake mechanisms or electronic parking brakes. Our technicians are experienced across all common systems and makes.
includes: OEM-quality rear brake discs and pads fitted as a set
EPB motor retraction and system calibration where required
Integrated drum handbrake mechanism inspected and serviced
Road test and handbrake function check on completion

name: Tyre Supply & Fitting
description: We source and fit tyres across all budget, mid-range and premium categories for cars, SUVs and light vans. We advise on the right tyre for your vehicle and usage, and always balance and fit in pairs to the same axle.
includes: Tyre sourced to match vehicle speed and load ratings
New valve fitted as standard
Fitted, balanced and torqued to manufacturer specification
Old tyre disposed of responsibly

name: Wheel Balancing
description: Wheel imbalance causes steering vibration, accelerates tyre wear and increases rolling resistance. If you feel vibration at speed or have recently had a tyre fitted, balancing should be checked as a matter of course.
includes: Each wheel dynamically balanced on our computer balancing machine
Balance weights added or adjusted for correct static and dynamic balance
Suitable for all tyre sizes including large alloy wheels
Completed while-you-wait in most cases

name: Laser 4-Wheel Alignment
description: Precision 4-wheel laser alignment to manufacturer specification corrects steering geometry that has shifted through use, kerbing or suspension wear. Misalignment causes uneven tyre wear, poor handling and increased fuel consumption.
includes: Full 4-wheel laser alignment measured against OEM specification
Toe, camber and caster adjusted where geometrically possible
Before and after alignment printout provided
Tyre wear pattern assessment and cause diagnosis included

name: TPMS Sensor Service
description: Tyre pressure monitoring sensors require periodic servicing or replacement, particularly after a tyre change. A dashboard TPMS warning that won't clear usually points to a faulty or depleted sensor — which we carry in stock for most common vehicles.
includes: TPMS fault code diagnosis across all sensors
Sensor replacement (individual or full set as required)
System reset and relearn procedure completed
Tyre pressures set to manufacturer specification before handover

name: Spark Plug Replacement
description: Worn or fouled spark plugs reduce combustion efficiency, causing rough running, reduced fuel economy, misfires and difficult cold starts. Replacement intervals vary — typically every 30,000 miles for copper plugs, up to 60,000 miles for iridium types.
includes: All spark plugs replaced as a complete set
Correct heat range and reach specified for your engine
Ignition leads and coil packs visually inspected
Engine management fault codes cleared if plug-related

name: Timing Belt & Water Pump Replacement
description: The timing belt is one of the most critical components in your engine — failure causes catastrophic and expensive damage with no warning. We strongly recommend replacing the water pump at the same time, as access requires the same strip-down.
includes: Timing belt, tensioner and idler pulley replaced as a set
Water pump replacement (strongly recommended at same time)
Coolant refreshed as part of the water pump procedure
Full visual engine bay inspection on completion

name: Clutch Replacement
description: A slipping, juddering or heavy clutch is a clear sign that replacement is due. We replace the complete clutch kit as standard — friction disc, pressure plate and release bearing — to ensure reliability and avoid early repeat repairs.
includes: Full clutch kit replacement (disc, pressure plate and release bearing)
Flywheel inspected; resurfaced or replaced if required
Gearbox oil level checked and topped up on completion
Road tested to confirm correct engagement and smooth operation

name: Manual Gearbox Service
description: Gearbox oil degrades over time, increasing wear and causing stiffer, noisier gear changes. Regular oil changes significantly extend gearbox life — typically recommended every 40,000 to 60,000 miles depending on vehicle and usage.
includes: Drain and refill with manufacturer-specified gearbox fluid
Gearbox breather and seals inspected for leaks
Gear selection and synchromesh function checked
Linkage adjustment carried out if required

name: Automatic & DSG Gearbox Service
description: Automatic and DSG transmissions operate at high temperatures and are more demanding on fluid than manuals. Neglecting fluid changes leads to hesitation, harsh or delayed shifts and, ultimately, premature transmission failure.
includes: Transmission fluid drain and refill to manufacturer specification
Sump filter replacement where applicable
DSG mechatronic and clutch pack adaptation reset where required
Full shift quality assessment and fault code check

name: DPF Service (Diesel)
description: A blocked diesel particulate filter causes power loss, increased fuel consumption and an engine management warning light. We offer a professional regeneration service that avoids filter replacement in many cases, saving significant cost.
includes: Diagnostic scan to confirm DPF blockage and soot load percentage
Forced regeneration using professional DPF cleaning equipment
DPF pressure differential and temperature sensor check
Fault code clearance and road test to confirm regeneration

name: EGR Valve Service (Diesel)
description: The EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) valve can become heavily carbon-fouled on diesel engines, causing rough idle, poor throttle response and increased emissions. Professional cleaning often restores full function without the cost of replacement.
includes: EGR valve removed and inspected for carbon build-up
Professional ultrasonic or chemical cleaning carried out
EGR cooler and intake manifold inspected for associated blockage
Full fault code scan and system test after refitting

name: Suspension Health Check
description: A thorough visual and physical inspection of every steering and suspension component. Essential after a pothole impact, if you're experiencing unusual handling or noise, or as part of MOT preparation — often uncovers wear before it becomes a safety concern.
includes: Front and rear shock absorber function and condition test
All bushes, ball joints and drop links inspected for play and wear
Steering rack, column and track rod ends checked
Subframe and mounting point condition assessed

name: Shock Absorber Replacement
description: Failed shock absorbers increase stopping distances, cause excessive body roll and leave the vehicle feeling unsettled. We always replace fronts or rears as a pair to maintain balanced handling and even tyre wear across the axle.
includes: Shock absorbers replaced as a matched pair (front or rear)
Top mounts and bump stops inspected and replaced if worn
Wheel alignment check recommended after rear replacement
Road test on completion to verify handling improvement

name: Coil Spring Replacement
description: A broken or sagged coil spring affects ride height, handling and creates rubbing or clunking over uneven surfaces. Springs must always be replaced as a pair on the same axle to prevent uneven ride height and handling characteristics.
includes: Springs replaced as a matched pair on the same axle
Spring seat, bump stop and dust cover condition checked
Vehicle ride height verified after replacement
4-wheel alignment recommended after any spring replacement

name: Wheel Bearing Replacement
description: Wheel bearing noise — typically a rumbling or growling that changes with cornering load — worsens progressively and can lead to serious safety risks if neglected. We carry a wide range of OEM-quality bearings for all common makes.
includes: Faulty wheel bearing identified and replaced
Hub and carrier condition inspected (replacement if worn)
ABS sensor cleaned and operation verified
Wheel torqued to manufacturer specification and road tested

name: Track Rod End & Steering Linkage
description: Worn track rod ends cause imprecise steering, uneven tyre wear and an MOT failure. Replacement must be followed by a 4-wheel alignment to re-establish correct toe settings — which we carry out as standard after all steering linkage work.
includes: Worn track rod end(s) removed and replaced
Lock nut torqued to manufacturer specification
4-wheel laser alignment carried out after replacement
Steering feel, self-centring and play verified on road test

name: Anti-Roll Bar Links & Bushes
description: Worn anti-roll bar drop links and bushes are a common cause of clunking over bumps and increased body roll. They are also a frequent MOT advisory. Replacement is straightforward and makes an immediate improvement to handling refinement.
includes: Anti-roll bar drop links replaced (front and/or rear as required)
Anti-roll bar mounting bushes replaced where worn
Steering and suspension torqued to manufacturer specification
Road test to confirm elimination of noise and improved stability

name: Full Diagnostic Health Check
description: Our multi-brand diagnostic equipment reads fault codes across all vehicle control systems — engine, transmission, ABS, airbags, body control and more. The most effective first step when any warning light appears or a fault develops.
includes: Full scan across all available vehicle control modules
Live data readings and fault code interpretation
Written diagnostic report with fault summary
Clear advice on required repairs and recommended priority

name: Engine Management Light Investigation
description: An illuminated EML can indicate anything from a minor sensor fault to a serious mechanical issue. We carry out a targeted diagnostic scan to pinpoint the root cause and advise on the repair before any work is carried out.
includes: Targeted OBD-II scan and fault code interpretation
Live engine data analysis where relevant to the fault
Root cause identified and confirmed before repair quotation
Fault codes cleared after any rectification work

name: Battery Test & Replacement
description: Modern vehicles place high demands on their batteries, particularly those with start-stop systems and large electrical loads. A weak battery causes hard starting and electrical gremlins well before complete failure. We test battery condition while you wait.
includes: Battery health, cold cranking amps (CCA) and state-of-charge tested
Charging circuit and alternator output tested simultaneously
OEM-quality replacement battery fitted if required
Battery registration completed on vehicles that require it (BMW, Mercedes etc.)

name: Alternator Testing & Replacement
description: A failing alternator drains the battery, causes electrical warning lights and eventually leaves you stranded. We test the full charging system under load and can source and fit replacement alternators for all common makes and models.
includes: Full charging circuit load test carried out
Alternator output voltage and current verified
Drive belt and tensioner condition inspected
Battery recharged and full system verified after replacement

name: Air Conditioning Regas
description: Air conditioning systems lose refrigerant gradually — most require regassing every two to three years to maintain cooling performance. We handle both R134a (pre-2017 vehicles) and the newer R1234yf refrigerant used in modern cars.
includes: Full AC system pressure test and leak check
Refrigerant recovered, vacuum held and system recharged
Correct refrigerant type and manufacturer-specified quantity used
Cooling performance and compressor operation verified on completion

name: Air Conditioning Full Service
description: Beyond a standard regas, our full AC service includes inspection and cleaning of the system's internal components. Recommended where performance is reduced, odours are present, or the system hasn't been serviced in several years.
includes: Full regas with correct refrigerant type and quantity
Evaporator and condenser performance check
Anti-bacterial cabin treatment to eliminate musty odours
Compressor, expansion valve and pressure switch operation verified

name: Coolant System Flush
description: Engine coolant degrades over time, losing its ability to prevent corrosion and regulate operating temperature. Overdue coolant is a leading contributor to head gasket and water pump failures — most manufacturers recommend a change every three to five years.
includes: Full coolant drain, flush and refill with manufacturer-specified mix
Cooling system pressure test to check for leaks
Thermostat function and opening temperature verified
Hoses, clips and water pump condition inspected during procedure

name: Cabin Air Filter Replacement
description: The cabin filter captures dust, pollen, bacteria and particulates before they enter the interior. A blocked filter reduces HVAC airflow, increases blower motor load and causes musty odours. Typically recommended every 12 months or 12,000 miles.
includes: Old cabin filter removed and condition inspected
New OEM-quality cabin filter fitted
Filter housing cleaned before installation
AC recirculation and fresh air modes tested on completion

name: Exhaust Inspection & Repair
description: Blowing joints, rattles and emission failures often result from corroded gaskets, cracked sections or failed mounting rubbers. We inspect the full system and carry out targeted repairs where complete replacement is not required.
includes: Full exhaust system inspection from manifold to tailpipe
Blow points, joint condition and mounting rubbers assessed
Welded repairs or section replacement carried out as appropriate
Emissions function test on completion

name: Exhaust Section Replacement
description: When a single section of the exhaust system fails — centre pipe, middle box or rear box — targeted replacement is more cost-effective than a full system. We source matched sections for all common makes and carry out most replacements while-you-wait.
includes: Failed section identified and removed
OEM or quality aftermarket replacement sourced and fitted
All joint gaskets renewed as standard
Full system check and emissions function verified on completion

name: Catalytic Converter Replacement
description: A failed catalytic converter causes an emissions failure and engine management light. Failure is often caused by misfires, oil consumption or physical damage — we diagnose and address the root cause before replacement to prevent recurrence.
includes: Full diagnostic scan to confirm catalytic converter failure
Root cause identified and addressed before replacement
OEM-quality replacement fitted with new gaskets and hardware
Fault codes cleared and emissions levels verified after replacement
